blocks.text: Nova Scotia is the second jurisdiction, with Canada and NATO as customers. Kourou stands for ESA, institutional customers and near-equatorial orbits. SaxaVord and Esrange are SSO backups if Andøya goes down. Santa Maria offers mid inclinations from EU soil, so far suborbital only.

blocks.title: Core message

blocks.text: One pad at Andøya manages only about {{portfolio_chain:A_rampe_wetter:value|num|0}} launches per year after weather, while break-even is at {{break_even_ops}}. The second pad (Andøya Pad 2 or Nova Scotia) is the most important step. The Vaterstetten factory (capacity {{facts:fa_003:value_num}} per year) is sufficient for that.
blocks.title: Cadence before footprint

blocks.text: Contract in place since 7 Jul 2026, first launch planned for 2028, Canadian launch legislation (C-28) still pending. Money only against milestones: licence, pad handover, first launch.
blocks.title: Nova Scotia as insurance, not as a growth engine

blocks.text: Kourou only for ESA and institutional customers. SaxaVord as an emergency backup for SSO without Norway.
